correctness.rationale: Under the published reduced Swiatkowski comparison for a graph without isolated vertices, the weight-three degree-three chain group is Z^9120 and there is no C4. The exact signed boundary is independently regenerated by VERIFY.py. A rank-9099 certificate mod 3 for the complementary columns and twenty-one integral null cycles with an identity submatrix imply a complete integral kernel basis of rank twenty-one. Exhaustive cycle enumeration finds exactly twenty disjoint triples of simple hexagons, each producing an integral torus cycle. Their 21-by-20 coefficient matrix has a determinant-one 20-by-20 minor, proving the product-torus subgroup is primitive with rank-one free quotient. Exhaustive mod-two boundary rank 9094 and integral free H3 rank 21 imply H2[2] = (Z/2)^5 by universal coefficients. The verifier reconstructs all matrices and certificates from the two embedded source files. The general chain-model equivalence is used as a published theorem rather than re-proved.

value.rationale: The Desargues incidence graph is a canonical symmetric, nonplanar 20-vertex cubic graph. Product three-tori made from independent motion along disjoint simple cycles are the natural topological generators to test. Their complete primitive rank-twenty lattice occupies a proper corank-one direct summand of the twenty-one-dimensional integral top homology, producing a concrete nonproduct top class and distinguishing a missing free class from finite-index torsion. The additional five-dimensional degree-two order-two subgroup is a motivically related integral phenomenon invisible to rational invariants. The calculation is precise and reproducible, not an arbitrary chosen subset.
